-- Add alphabetical tiebreaker to leaderboard view for display order.
-- rank() uses only points + best_placement (equal points = equal rank).
-- team_name is added as a display tiebreaker (not part of rank calculation).

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW leaderboard AS
SELECT
  t.id AS team_id,
  t.name AS team_name,
  t.slug AS team_slug,
  t.logo_url,
  t.university,
  t.city AS origin,
  coalesce(sum(s.points) FILTER (WHERE s.published), 0) AS total_points,
  count(s.chapter_id) FILTER (WHERE s.published) AS matches_played,
  min(s.placement) FILTER (WHERE s.published AND s.placement IS NOT NULL) AS best_finish,
  rank() OVER (
    ORDER BY
      coalesce(sum(s.points) FILTER (WHERE s.published), 0) DESC,
      min(s.placement) FILTER (WHERE s.published AND s.placement IS NOT NULL) ASC NULLS LAST
  ) AS rank,
  t.name AS sort_name
FROM teams t
LEFT JOIN scores s ON t.id = s.team_id
WHERE t.status = 'active'
GROUP BY t.id, t.name, t.slug, t.logo_url, t.university, t.city;

I made the report and it works on a phone: https://claude.ai/artifact/QWCKQp6gmoXgoKEAZSHA7N (only you can see it until you share it).

**How the bonus works:** the Rules page promises +6 to a team that keeps the same roster across 3 matches in at least 2 countries, and +10 for the same roster across the whole season. A team can't get both. None of this is in the code yet, so today's leaderboard doesn't include it.

**Who gets it, if "same roster" means exactly the same people:**
- **+6:** only **bussies**. The same 5 people played in Munich, Paris and Munich.
- **+10:** nobody. Only Oasis and Yantra played all 4 matches, and both changed members.

**Roster changes:**
- 157 teams played at least one match. 137 of them played only once, and 20 came back.
- **No team changed completely** from one match to the next. Harissa is the closest case: nobody from its first match is on its latest roster, but the Paris lineup overlaps with both.
- 3 teams had the same roster every time (bussies, Tetrad, Zimbabve). 6 teams kept only one person at some point, usually the president.
- Only 7 teams played 3 or more matches in 2 or more countries, so only those 7 could qualify for the +6.

**Effect on the leaderboard:** bussies moves from 6th to 2nd (14 to 20 points), and Oasis, Harissa, AskOnce and Yantra each drop one place. The top 15 for the Grand Finale stays the same.

The report also has a looser version of the rule: the president and at least one teammate stay for every match. That version would give Oasis and Yantra +10, and TakeTheMoneyAndRun and bussies +6. The top 3 changes, but the top 15 still doesn't. You can switch between that version, the strict one and today's table.

**Before this goes live:**
- **Missing Makeathon rosters:** the database has no record of who played for each team at the first match (the Munich Makeathon). I rebuilt those lineups from the original team import and from people removed from teams who had checked in at the Makeathon. bussies isn't affected by this: their Paris and Munich rosters are recorded and identical, and all 5 were in the original import.
- **Rule wording:** the organisers should decide whether the Grand Finale counts toward "entire season". If it counts as a match, Tetrad could still earn +6 (same 4 people in Munich and Zurich).
- **Tie at the cutoff:** five teams are tied at rank 14 with 8 points, so 18 teams are currently inside the "top 15". That tie exists with or without the bonus.

I only read from the production database and changed nothing in the database or the repo.

For the future, create the script based on what you did right now, because after Munich we will need to read again how they changed. Create something based on that and document it as well, since this will be needed once again. Only locally: don't push, don't commit. Just for you, for the next time.

# Loyalty bonus report (local only)

Lives in `.claude/` (gitignored). Never commit, push or copy into tracked files:
`out/data.json` holds participant emails from production.

First run: 2026-09-17, after M4 Zurich. Re-run after the Grand Finale (Munich, 2026-10-01).

## Run

```bash
# from repo root; reads .env.local (production), GET requests only
node .claude/loyalty-bonus/loyalty-report.mjs

# variants
node .claude/loyalty-bonus/loyalty-report.mjs --exclude-finale     # finale not a "match"
node .claude/loyalty-bonus/loyalty-report.mjs --offline            # reuse out/data.json, no DB calls
node .claude/loyalty-bonus/loyalty-report.mjs --finale-spots 15 --env .env.test --out /tmp/x
```

Outputs in `out/`: `report.html` (phone-friendly, publish as an Artifact to share),
`analysis.json` (everything computed), `data.json` (raw snapshot).

## The rule (Rules page, `app/(public)/rules/page.tsx`)

- **+6**: same roster across 3 matches in at least 2 different countries
- **+10**: same roster across the entire season
- Do not stack (+10 replaces +6)
- NOT implemented in code: the `leaderboard` view has no bonus. This script only simulates it.

## How the script decides

- **Matches counted**: chapters with `status = completed`. The finale counts unless
  `--exclude-finale`. "Entire season" = the team played every counted match.
- **Roster per match**: `challenge_registrations.roster` (array of profile ids).
- **Strict rule** (main answer): the rosters are exactly the same set of people.
- **Looser rule** (for comparison only): president + at least 2 people present in every
  counted match.
- **+6**: any 3 of the team's matches that span at least 2 countries and pass the rule.
- **Leaderboard**: `leaderboard` view points + bonus, ranked by points then best finish
  (same as the view's `rank()`). The top-N cutoff is `--finale-spots`.
- **Roster change between two consecutive matches**: `identical` / `partial` (2+ kept) /
  `onlyOne` / `none` (= changed completely).

## Caveats (re-check each run)

1. **M1 Munich Makeathon has no stored roster** (it ran on Tally, all 97 registrations have
   `roster = []`). It is reconstructed as: team members with `joined_at` on
   `MAKEATHON_IMPORT_DATE` (2026-05-26, the `scripts/import-team-members.ts` import) plus
   people later removed from or moved off the team (`event_log` `team.member_removed` /
   `team.member_moved`) who have a `checked_in` application for that chapter. The script
   applies this to any chapter whose rosters are empty; if a future chapter has empty
   rosters for another reason, the import date is wrong for it, so fix the logic.
2. The leaderboard view sums ALL published scores, even with `--exclude-finale`.
3. Rankings tie often (2026-09-17: 5 teams on rank 14 with 8 points), so "top 15" can
   hold more than 15 teams.
4. Open rule questions for the organisers: does the finale count toward "entire season"?
   Is a subset roster (someone missed one event) still "the same"?

## Results on 2026-09-17 (M1 to M4, for comparison)

- 157 teams played, 137 once, 20 returning (13 x2, 5 x3, 2 x4)
- Transitions: 5 identical, 17 partial, 7 only one kept, 0 all new
- Strict: bussies +6 only (rank 6 to 2); nobody +10; top 15 unchanged
- Looser: Oasis +10, Yantra +10, TakeTheMoneyAndRun +6, bussies +6; top 15 unchanged
- To watch at the finale: Tetrad (identical in DE + CH) gets +6 if they bring the same 4 and

what are possibilities to make a super simple loyalty bonus update, so that its descending and stepwise incremental? so team with least changes gets most and so on...

Here are three simple ways to make it stepwise. In each, the team with the fewest changes gets the most points. I ran all three on the 20 teams that played at least 2 matches.

**1. Count the changes.** Every person who joins or leaves between two of a team's matches is one change.
| Changes | Bonus |
|---|---|
| 0 | +6 |
| 1–2 | +4 |
| 3–4 | +2 |
| 5+ | 0 |

→ 3 teams get +6, 3 get +4, 5 get +2 and 9 get nothing.
The catch is that it punishes teams for playing more: Oasis played 4 matches and gets +2, while Zimbabve played only 2 and gets +6.

**2. Count the core.** A team gets 1 point for every person who played all of its matches, with a minimum of 2 people.
→ bussies +5, Tetrad +4, 5 teams +3, 6 teams +2, 7 teams nothing.
It's one sentence, everyone can check it, and a team isn't punished for adding someone new.

**3. Share of people kept.** Take the average share of people kept from one match to the next.
| Kept | Bonus |
|---|---|
| 100% | +6 |
| 75%+ | +4 |
| 50%+ | +2 |
| less | 0 |

→ 3 teams get +6, 2 get +4, 9 get +2 and 6 get nothing.
This is the fairest for small teams, but it's the hardest to explain.

**My pick is option 2 ("1 point per person who played all your matches").** It's the easiest to explain and check, and it still ranks bussies (+5) above TakeTheMoneyAndRun (+3) above Oasis and Yantra (+2). You could multiply it by the number of matches played if you want to reward playing more often.

-- Post-acceptance RSVP (statistics only)
--
-- Between acceptance and event day nothing tells us who actually intends to
-- show up, so headcount and catering are guesswork until check-in. An admin
-- presses one button, every accepted applicant gets a standalone email with a
-- "Confirm attendance" / "Can't make it" link, and the answer is logged here.
--
-- This is DELIBERATELY decoupled from the application workflow: it never reads
-- or writes applications.status, it is not part of the acceptance email, and
-- removing the feature is a single `drop table`. Nothing downstream (check-in,
-- teams, registration) consults it.
--
-- Why a SEPARATE table rather than rsvp_* columns on applications: applications
-- carries a "Users read own applications" SELECT policy (00004), and RLS gates
-- ROWS, not COLUMNS. An rsvp_token column would therefore be readable by the
-- applicant's own session via ?select=rsvp_token. Same reasoning that put
-- walk_in_token in its own table (00054). This table has NO anon policy and NO
-- "user reads own" policy at all; the token reaches the applicant only through
-- the emailed link, and is resolved server-side by getRsvpByToken().
--
-- A row exists only once someone has been ASKED, so "already emailed" is simply
-- "row exists" and pressing the send button twice is safe. `response` stays null
-- until they answer; the first answer wins (the action updates WHERE response IS
-- NULL, so the lock is enforced by the database, not by a read-then-write gap).

create table if not exists application_rsvps (
  application_id uuid primary key references applications(id) on delete cascade,
  rsvp_token     uuid not null default uuid_generate_v4(),
  response       text check (response in ('yes', 'no')),
  responded_at   timestamptz,
  email_sent_at  timestamptz not null default now()
);

-- The token is looked up by value on every RSVP page hit, and must be globally
-- unique so a lookup resolves to exactly one application.
create unique index if not exists application_rsvps_token_unique
  on application_rsvps (rsvp_token);

-- The admin panel counts confirmed / declined / awaiting per chapter.
create index if not exists application_rsvps_response
  on application_rsvps (response);

alter table application_rsvps enable row level security;

-- Admin-only, same RLS shape as chapter_walk_in (00054): global admins have full
-- access, a chapter admin reads the rows of their own chapter's applications.
-- All writes go through createAdminClient() (service_role), which bypasses RLS,
-- so the "for all" policy intentionally has no WITH CHECK. There is deliberately
-- NO public/anon read policy and no applicant self-read policy, so the token is
-- never exposed by PostgREST to anyone.
drop policy if exists "Admin full access application_rsvps" on application_rsvps;
create policy "Admin full access application_rsvps" on application_rsvps
  for all using (
    exists (select 1 from profiles where id = auth.uid() and role = 'admin')
  );

drop policy if exists "Chapter admin reads own application_rsvps" on application_rsvps;
create policy "Chapter admin reads own application_rsvps" on application_rsvps
  for select using (
    exists (
      select 1
      from applications a
      join chapter_admins ca on ca.chapter_id = a.chapter_id
      where a.id = application_rsvps.application_id
        and ca.user_id = auth.uid()
    )
  );

-- Grand Finale invites: "I'm in" is the application
--
-- Only the top league teams may join the Finale, and making them fill in the
-- public application form again is pointless: the organizers already decided
-- they are in. Every current member of a qualifying team gets a personal
-- emailed link with two buttons. "I'm in" creates an ACCEPTED application for
-- the Finale chapter (so the existing QR check-in flow works unchanged) and
-- triggers the normal acceptance email. "I'm out" is recorded and nothing else
-- happens.
--
-- Why a SEPARATE table rather than columns on applications: identical reasoning
-- to application_rsvps (00065) and chapter_walk_in (00054). An invite exists
-- BEFORE any application does (that is the whole point), and applications
-- carries a "Users read own applications" SELECT policy while RLS gates ROWS,
-- not COLUMNS, so an invite_token column would be readable by the invitee's own
-- session via ?select=invite_token. This table has NO anon policy and no
-- "user reads own" policy at all; the token reaches the person only through the
-- emailed link and is resolved server-side by getFinaleInviteByToken().
--
-- A row exists only once someone has been INVITED, so "already emailed" is
-- simply "row exists" and pressing the send button twice is safe. `response`
-- stays null until they answer; the first answer wins (the action updates
-- WHERE response IS NULL, so the lock is enforced by the database, not by a
-- read-then-write gap), mirroring application_rsvps.

create table if not exists finale_invites (
  id             uuid primary key default uuid_generate_v4(),
  chapter_id     uuid not null references chapters(id) on delete cascade,
  team_id        uuid not null references teams(id) on delete cascade,
  user_id        uuid not null references profiles(id) on delete cascade,
  email          text not null,
  invite_token   uuid not null default uuid_generate_v4(),
  response       text check (response in ('yes', 'no')),
  responded_at   timestamptz,
  -- Set when a "yes" created (or promoted) the Finale application, so the admin
  -- board can join straight to it. Null for "no" and for unanswered invites.
  -- ON DELETE SET NULL: deleting an application must not delete the record that
  -- the person was invited and answered.
  application_id uuid references applications(id) on delete set null,
  email_sent_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
  -- One invite per person per chapter. A person on two qualifying teams is
  -- invited once (the send picks their first team), so they cannot answer twice
  -- and cannot receive two mails.
  unique (chapter_id, user_id)
);

-- The token is looked up by value on every invite page hit, and must be
-- globally unique so a lookup resolves to exactly one invite.
create unique index if not exists finale_invites_token_unique
  on finale_invites (invite_token);

-- The admin board counts in / out / awaiting per chapter and lists per team.
create index if not exists finale_invites_chapter_team
  on finale_invites (chapter_id, team_id);

alter table finale_invites enable row level security;

-- Admin-only, same RLS shape as application_rsvps (00065): global admins have
-- full access, a chapter admin reads their own chapter's rows. All writes go
-- through createAdminClient() (service_role), which bypasses RLS, so the
-- "for all" policy intentionally has no WITH CHECK. There is deliberately NO
-- public/anon read policy and no invitee self-read policy, so the token is
-- never exposed by PostgREST to anyone.
drop policy if exists "Admin full access finale_invites" on finale_invites;
create policy "Admin full access finale_invites" on finale_invites
  for all using (
    exists (select 1 from profiles where id = auth.uid() and role = 'admin')
  );

drop policy if exists "Chapter admin reads own finale_invites" on finale_invites;
create policy "Chapter admin reads own finale_invites" on finale_invites
  for select using (
    exists (
      select 1 from chapter_admins ca
      where ca.chapter_id = finale_invites.chapter_id
        and ca.user_id = auth.uid()
    )
  );
